patterns.usage_note: Counterfactual ところ: the event was on the verge of happening but in the end did not, so it is typically set up by 危[あぶ]なく, もう少しで or あやうく. This near-miss reading needs the dictionary form in front (するところ); after the past tense (〜たところ) the same noun instead means 'had just done it'. Past ところだった／ところであった reports the averted event, while present ところだ describes something still teetering on the brink; とこ is the clipped conversational shape.

examples.ruby: もう少[すこ]しで電車[でんしゃ]に乗[の]り遅[おく]れるとこだ。
examples.english: I came within a hair of missing my train.

examples.ruby: あぶない、コップを落[お]とすとこだ。
examples.english: Careful, you're about to drop that glass.

examples.ruby: 一歩[いっぽ]間違[まちが]えば大[おお]けがをするところだ。
examples.english: One wrong step and you'd be badly hurt.
